_comment: Reviewed holes in the cross-language artifact-role parity gate
(datrix/scripts/test/artifact-role-parity-gate.ps1). Each entry names one
(example, domain, language) coordinate where that language's blessed baseline
has zero files matching the domain's structural_pattern, even though >= 1
other blessed language for the SAME example has one. This is a genuine,
reviewed gap -- never a suppression of an unexplained finding.
Every entry below was investigated by reading the actual blessed manifest
paths and the declared structural_pattern before being recorded. Two
further categories of apparent divergence turned out to be fixable in the
gate's OWN classifier rather than needing an exemption at all (see
_pattern_specificity's most-specific-match tie-break and
_PACKAGE_MARKER_BASENAMES in artifact_role_parity.py) -- a shallower
sibling domain's glob no longer steals credit from a deeper, more
specific one, and a bare package-init marker (e.g. __init__.py) is never
credited to any domain. What remains below are the genuine gaps:
(1) dotnet's helper/Support/*.cs output is emitted only when the DSL
invokes a gating builtin category or an extension that declares its
own Support helper; python/typescript/java instead always emit
baseline helper-utility scaffolding regardless of DSL content.
expected_count is a pinned, reviewed value: change it only in the same
change that adds or removes an entry.

exemptions.reason: dotnet emits Support/*.cs only when the DSL invokes a gating builtin category or an extension that declares its own Support helper. Verified against the real generated output (dotnet.sha256 blessed manifest): zero Support/*.cs paths. Verified against all five DSL sources: no Auth./Json./Validator./Request. builtin call, no Log.withContext/setLevel, no Crypto.* call, no extension usage, and no Geo/GeoShape builtin -- the 'Geo' matches are the user-declared GeoCoordinate struct and a name literal, and the 'request.' matches are the lowercase endpoint request parameter, not the Request. builtin namespace. python's blessed manifest holds three _datrix_helpers.py regardless of DSL content. A genuine per-language boilerplate-emission design difference, not a missing capability.

Verified against the real generated output (dotnet.sha256 blessed manifest): zero `Support/*.cs` paths. Verified against the DSL source (loan-service.dtrx/member-service.dtrx/common.dtrx): no Auth./Json./Validator./Request. builtin calls (the `request.bookId`/`request.memberId` occurrences are references to an inter-service call's own response variable named `request`, not `Request.*` builtin property-access calls), no Log.withContext/setLevel, no Geo/GeoShape/Crypto.sign, no extension usage, no Crypto.* call at all. python's blessed manifest always emits _datrix_helpers.py regardless of DSL content -- the same genuine per-language boilerplate-emission design difference the other entries in this file record, not a missing capability.

dotnet emits Support/*.cs only when the DSL invokes a gating builtin category (Auth/JSON/Validator/Request/Log) or an extension that declares its own Support helper (e.g. the geo extension, where dotnet's Support/GeoHelpers.cs is present and this domain is not exempted for that example). This example invokes none of those, so dotnet's blessed baseline holds zero Support files. python/typescript/java instead always emit baseline helper-utility scaffolding (_datrix_helpers.py, _archiveHelpers.ts, MapSupport.java) regardless of DSL content. A genuine per-language boilerplate-emission design difference, not a missing capability.

Verified against the real generated output, the DSL source, and typescript's own generator code: this example's only `discovery { }` block is empty (auto-configured service discovery infrastructure, no named dependent service inside it) and no `uses` directive or `extern service` declaration appears anywhere in its DSL sources -- `service.depends_on()` (service_accessors.py:269-294, merging `discovery.dependencies` and resolved `uses_directives`) is therefore empty, so dotnet's `DotnetClientGenerator` (gated on `service.depends_on()`) correctly emits zero `Clients/*.cs` files. typescript's blessed manifest DOES carry `src/clients/*.ts` files here regardless (e.g. `{service}-client.ts`), because typescript's OWN `client` domain generator (`ClientGenerator.generate_for_service`, generators/api/client_generator.py:31-55) emits exactly one self-referencing HTTP client stub per SERVICE, unconditionally, with no `depends_on()` gate or loop over dependencies at all -- `simple = extract_simple_name(service.name)` names the file after the service itself, not after a dependency. This is a genuine per-language boilerplate-emission design difference -- the same shape the `helper` entries elsewhere in this file record, with typescript playing the unconditional-emitter role this time -- not a missing capability.
